lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | Aug 2022 - Jul 2024
- Owned the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards across two major releases and the on-call rotation that used them.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases, adding automated regression checks that shortened release cycles from 2 weeks to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: Add a headline or summary that states the target role.
items.because: Readers have to infer whether the target is ML engineering, agent systems, or general software engineering.

items.says: Make the progression from robotics software into ML and agent work more explicit.
items.because: That transition is the résumé’s strongest story but is not easy enough to see.

items.says: Standardize the date format across the résumé.
Standardize separator formatting.
The experience entries are not in reverse chronological order.
items.because: The Mobility Systems internship ended later than the Eastern Robotics job.

items.says: Make the overlap among the master’s program, internship, and projects easier to understand.
items.because: Clear ordering and formatting can prevent readers from misreading the dates.

items.says: Consider adding location or work authorization if relevant to the target roles.
items.because: Neither is necessary in every résumé.

items.says: Clarify the scope of ownership, especially of the on-call rotation.
items.because: The bullet could be read as claiming ownership of the whole rotation.

items.says: Say what improved because of the dashboards or rotation.
items.because: The bullet establishes responsibility but not much impact.

items.says: Check that the before-and-after p95 figures were measured under comparable conditions.
Clarify whether the shorter release cycle covered all model releases or one workflow.
items.because: The scope of the quantified result is unclear.

items.says: Split or substantially narrow the migration bullet.
items.because: It combines several responsibilities and obscures the main accomplishment.

items.says: Clarify which change removed the nightly backlog.
items.because: The result should be distinguished from the onboarding and on-call work.

items.says: Make the scope of “30” unambiguous.
Explain what “800+ sensor signals per case” means.
Give the comparison period or backlog measure behind the 68% reduction.
items.because: The measurement is not fully clear.

items.says: Clarify the triage branch’s attribution to the backlog reduction.
items.because: The result’s attribution is not fully clear.

items.says: Clarify what the domain adapter was applied to.
Explain how the held-out evaluation was kept separate from training or tuning.
items.because: Technical readers need to assess whether the improvement is meaningful and trustworthy.

items.says: Explain how dynamic batching reduced latency for single-request inference.
items.because: A technical reader may wonder how those details fit together.

items.says: Give measurement context such as hardware or serving conditions.
items.because: It would help readers interpret the 40% p95 latency reduction.

items.says: Fix the sentence’s missing clear subject.
items.because: Readers cannot tell who or what produced the result.

items.says: Specify the comparison behind the 5% latency reduction.
items.because: The modest result needs context.

items.says: Define what “end-to-end latency” includes.
items.because: The modest result needs context.

items.says: Give observable training behavior or a metric supporting “stabilised.”
items.because: The stability claim needs evidence.

items.says: Explain why one rollout per prompt helped in this setting.
items.because: That strategy may raise questions about reward-signal quality and diversity.

items.says: Clarify what the reviewers adopted.
Clarify how broadly the runbook was used.
items.because: That would show how the work affected team practice.

items.says: Add a project link if one is public and useful for verification.
Replace the vague delivery-and-outcomes claim with a concrete, measured change or remove it.
items.because: The bullet does not say what changed or how it was measured.

items.says: Reword the “AI-first” phrasing.
items.because: It risks sounding like a generic slogan.

items.says: The 900 ms to 600 ms change is a 33.3% reduction, not 50%.
items.because: The incorrect percentage harms credibility.

items.says: Give the benchmark or workload behind the latency measurement.
items.because: Readers need context to interpret it.

items.says: Address how caching completed answers affected correctness or freshness, if relevant.
The change from 71% to 83% is 12 percentage points, not simply 12%.
Give the benchmark sample size or evaluation conditions.
items.because: Readers need to judge the result and its robustness.

items.says: Identify the framework or link to the upstream contribution if possible.
items.because: A reviewer could then verify the work.

items.says: Make the eight metrics distinguishable in the résumé or linked materials.
Clarify what the correlation compared the evaluator’s behavior against.
items.because: Otherwise, the number is difficult to interpret.

items.says: Specify whether 0.89 is Kendall’s tau or another statistic.
items.because: Otherwise, the number is difficult to interpret.

items.says: Clarify your specific role in tracing and resolving the defects.
Give the nature or consequence of the defects.
items.because: “Stability,” “sourcing,” and “parameter handling” are broad categories.

items.says: Git is listed as a programming language, but it is a development tool.
items.because: The skills categories should let readers scan them accurately.

items.says: Add substantiated implementation tools to the skills section.
items.because: The work mentions CI, event queues, edge inference, caching, and model serving, but little of that stack appears in skills.

items.says: Move Kubernetes out of the “ML & Agents” category.
items.because: It sits awkwardly there.

items.says: Make sure the listed Kubernetes and GRPO skills are supported by the work shown.
items.because: They may invite questions about how deeply they were used.
